title: Operational Hayden–Preskill recovery: polar/QSVT-Petz decoder qualification

references.name: Petz Recovery through a Single Polar Transformation for Approximate Quantum Error Correction
references.role: QSVT polar sign implementation, no-postselection extension, spectral loss and diamond-distance bound.

references.name: Optimality Condition for the Petz Map
references.role: Necessary-and-sufficient Petz entanglement-fidelity optimality condition, with commuting-input specialization.

references.name: Simulating Floquet scrambling circuits on trapped-ion quantum computers
references.role: 20-qubit experimental Hayden–Preskill and OTOC reference; hardware comparison only.

claim_ceiling: Finite-dimensional channel and decoder-circuit qualification only. No macroscopic black-hole, gravitational, island/QES or quantum-advantage claim.

channel.scrambler: seeded Haar U(4) on M tensor B
channel.decoder_access_policy: The decoder receives only the declared regime input; for the assisted setup it is E tensor R. The remnant C is always inaccessible.
channel.seed_policy: frozen common seed schedule across all decoder families
channel.inaccessible_environment_description: The remaining black-hole remnant output after U acts on M tensor B; it is traced out and is unavailable to the decoder. In the literature cited for the assisted Hayden–Preskill decoder, this is the remnant output called C; the accessible old radiation is called B'_early there and is our R.

notation_mapping.local: M is the message; B is the initially entangled black-hole subsystem; R is the accessible early-radiation purifier; U(M tensor B) outputs E (newly accessible radiation) and C (remaining remnant). Decoder input is A=E tensor R.
notation_mapping.literature: In the cited Hayden-Preskill QSVT paper, the decoder input is D tensor B'_early; its inaccessible remnant output is C.
notation_mapping.equivalence: Local E tensor R corresponds to literature D tensor B'_early. Local C_remnant corresponds to literature C. The existing source identifier b_prime names local C_remnant, not literature B'_early.
notation_mapping.comparison_rule: Assisted and unassisted runs are distinct channels; compare only within matched access regimes.

decoder_families.claim: Channel-level recovery, no gate-level circuit cost.
Candidate decoder family, not a global optimality claim.

decoder_families.method: Independent SDP over recovery Choi matrices; use Petz-optimality theorem only when all hypotheses are satisfied.
Block-encode stacked Petz isometry operator; approximate its polar sign transform with an odd QSVT polynomial and extend to a recovery isometry without postselection.

qsvt_contract.polynomial: real odd p_theta(x) of degree at most 2k+1 approximates sign(x) on the declared nonzero scaled singular-value support
qsvt_contract.normalization: alpha is the declared block-encoding normalization and must be included in every receipt
qsvt_contract.spectrum_weighted_loss: I_theta = 1 - |sum_i lambda_i^2 p_theta(x_i)|^2 under the pinned reference convention
qsvt_contract.target_bound: Delta_theta <= sqrt(||sigma^{-1}||_infinity * I_theta); verify theorem hypotheses and exact normalization against the pinned preprint before implementing
qsvt_contract.postselection_experiment: Optional comparison only; report success probability and expected repetitions, and do not label the conditional branch deterministic or trace-preserving.

proposed_targets.comparisons: Matched channel, seed, decoder access, accuracy and resource budget.

negative_controls: compare entanglement-assisted E_tensor_R channel against unassisted E-only channel as though their decoder access sets matched
explicit_nonclaims: not a physical trapped-ion or other hardware result
not a macroscopic black-hole evaporation simulation
not a proof that rotated Petz is universally optimal
not an efficient decoder claim until resources are implemented and measured
the internal variable name b_prime denotes the inaccessible remnant C, not the literature's accessible early-radiation B-prime register
